notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act. The 26 September 2026 Texas Tribune article (republished at https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/us-should-err-side-innovation-ai-regulation-us-rep-arrington-says, which returned 403 to my fetch) was read through Click2Houston via a fetch tool that summarizes pages; the two quotes match the wording in the search results, but a reviewer should confirm them at the source. The same article quotes him saying "Zero risk means we lose" and "If that's the game we're going to play, we will lose"; these oppose a zero-risk approach to regulation but do not dismiss catastrophic risk, so they are not F. The article paraphrases him calling United Nations-style AI governance "disastrous" because he does not trust China; only the word was quoted, so it is not included as a statement. No source showed him sponsoring or co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (reported House cosponsors did not include him) or signing a House letter on AI risk of his own. An earlier run opened his official site: the 60 most recent press releases (late 2025 to 27 October 2026) contain no mention of AI. A 1 August 2025 Avalanche-Journal article republished on his site (https://arrington.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=3973) has him saying West Texas can power AI data centers; also D, not quoted. He is not seeking reelection; his term ends January 2027.
